0: Khlestakov, Osip, and later the Servant. KHLESTAKOV. Well?
2: KHLESTAKOV [claps his hands and wriggles in his chair]. Dinner, dinner, dinner!
3: SERVANT [with plates and napkin]. This is the last time the landlord will let you have dinner.
4: KHLESTAKOV. The landlord, the landlord! I spit on your landlord. What have you got there?
8: KHLESTAKOV. Nonsense! I won't take it. What does he mean by that? Ask him. It's not enough.
9: SERVANT. The landlord says it's too much.
10: KHLESTAKOV. Why is there no sauce?
12: KHLESTAKOV. Why not? I saw them preparing a whole lot when I passed through the kitchen. And in the dining-room this morning two short little men were eating salmon and lots of other things.
13: SERVANT. Well, you see, there is some and there isn't.
16: KHLESTAKOV. What, no salmon, no fish, no cutlets?
17: SERVANT. Only for the better kind of folk.
20: KHLESTAKOV. You measly suckling pig. Why can they eat and I not? Why the devil can't I eat, too? Am I not a guest the same as they?
21: SERVANT. No, not the same. That's plain.
23: SERVANT. That's easy. THEY pay, that's it.
24: KHLESTAKOV. I'm not going to argue with you, simpleton! [Ladles out the soup and begins to eat.] What, you call that soup? Simply hot water poured into a cup. No taste to it at all. It only stinks. I don't want it. Bring me some other soup.
25: SERVANT. All right. I'll take it away. The boss said if you didn't want it, you needn't take it.
26: KHLESTAKOV [putting his hand over the dishes]. Well, well, leave it alone, you fool. You may be used to treat other people this way, but I'm not that sort. I advise you not to try it on me. My God! What soup! [Goes on eating.] I don't think anybody in the world tasted such soup. Feathers floating on the top instead of butter. [Cuts the piece of chicken in the soup.] Oh, oh, oh! What a bird!—Give me the roast beef. There's a little soup left, Osip. Take it. [Cuts the meat.] What sort of roast beef is this? This isn't roast beef.
28: KHLESTAKOV. The devil knows, but it isn't roast beef. It's roast iron, not roast beef. [Eats.] Scoundrels! Crooks! The stuff they give you to eat! It makes your jaws ache to chew one piece of it. [Picks his teeth with his fingers.] Villains! It's as tough as the bark of a tree. I can't pull it out no matter how hard I try. Such meat is enough to ruin one's teeth. Crooks! [Wipes his mouth with the napkin.] Is there nothing else?
30: KHLESTAKOV. Scoundrels! Blackguards! They might have given some decent pastry, or something, the lazy good-for-nothings! Fleecing their guests! That's all they're good for.
31: [The Servant takes the dishes and carries them out accompanied by Osip.]
